label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
which_first: 03, because it gets to the four steps, the hold, the shared-team rule and a price within four printable pages, which is what I would hand to a co-founder.

03.one_line: Compact and practical: four steps, a stated cost, a stop rule and a team rule; I understand the factory's shape but not who answers when an agent errs.

10.one_line: Fuller and more honest, with the failures, the reviewer's limits and a worked shop example, but five pages of cast scenes before the method and three empty figure boxes.

tomorrow: Open one AI agent account, create an empty project with nothing private in it, and write the one page of rules for a single small task of my own (answering the questions clients ask most for the new company's site), including the line that it must stop and ask me before it promises anything. Then write a three-line brief and ask for a first draft by Friday.
would_share: yes, with my co-founder first, then a trusted contractor; the one page I would send is the final page of the 10 edition (pdf page 11, 'Your factory, starting tomorrow'), because the shop owner's sample rules and brief are what I can copy.
why_buy: It would need a real cost and hours account of a working team (even an estimate, plainly marked), an accountability section naming who signs off what, and the control descriptions an auditor would accept. The honest failures are what make me trust it.

best_page.why: Five steps with a worked example of rules and brief in a shop owner's words, a stated price, and the team rule with a named person able to lift the hold. This is the method, and it reads as something I could run.

worst_page.why: A page of mostly white space with a large 'figure to come' box and a creator's-problem story; it delays the method, and an unfinished placeholder on page one of the content weakens trust. The 3 edition's last page (pdf page 6), a list of internal file paths, is a close second.

one_change_before_the_editor_sees_it: On the 10 edition, pdf page 11, add one short 'what can go wrong and who answers' line beneath the five steps (the owner approves anything that leaves the building; the agent is never the one accountable), and a rough hours-per-week figure beside the $20 price, marked as an estimate if the record has none.
notes: Strengths for me: the plain admission that the day's own cost is not in the record, the reviewer line 'a second reading, not a second identity', the freeze failure (pdf page 9 of 10) and the hold rule with an owner. Weak spots: the scenes lean on cast personality and shorthand (a night owl, mortified, sheepish) where I want controls and owners; the 10 edition's 'what did not work' page is the best audit-style content but is buried; the 3 edition's source lists of internal file names are noise to a client; the series name and the 'up at three in the morning' tagline are close to the youth-culture shorthand I distrust, though the 'Generation ZX is not birth years' line softens it. Three figures are still marked to come in the 10 edition. Synthetic persona, a prompt for the team and not evidence.
